source.title: Poison to Detect: Detection of Targeted Overfitting in Federated Learning
source.citation: Soumia Zohra El Mestari et al., 2025
source.authors: Soumia Zohra El Mestari; M. Zuziak; Gabriele Lenzini

page_placements.theme: Retained training information can escape aggregate performance diagnostics

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. The header gives arXiv v3 dated 27 Jul 2026; the supplied catalog metadata lists year 2025.
record.tranche_reason: Studies targeted overfitting in federated learning, a different training setting and mechanism from the random-label experiments in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports overfitting and privacy measurements under malicious selective aggregation on client data. It does not test random labels, unstructured inputs, label-noise fractions, regularization effects, or the order in which clean and noisy patterns are learned. These results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures deliberately induced client-specific overfitting and membership-inference vulnerability in federated learning. It does not test any listed version. Its label-flipping procedure cyclically relabels selected examples from one class for detection; it does not measure fitting a completely random labeling, a corruption sweep, or clean-versus-noisy learning order.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that selective aggregation induces targeted overfitting and increases privacy exposure, and that client-side detection can identify it early. Their conclusion emphasizes strong single-client detection, with reduced fingerprinting performance when multiple clients are targeted. Membership inference is measured directly; model inversion and reconstruction are discussed as potential consequences.
record.recipe_differences: The paper induces targeted overfitting by selectively aggregating federated client updates and measures generalisation gaps and membership inference; it does not randomize training labels as in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that detection effectiveness varies with dataset, cohort composition, number of targeted clients, method parameters, and data heterogeneity.

fits_no_version.finding: Malicious selective aggregation increases MIA AUC from 0.511 to 0.701 on MNIST, 0.504 to 0.655 on EUROSAT, and 0.751 to 0.969 on PATHMNIST. Reported client-distribution loss gaps also increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective aggregation in federated learning can amplify targeted clients' relative fit and membership-inference vulnerability.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings on Privacy Enhancing Technologies 2026(4), as stated in the paper text
record.problems: The supplied text gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported MIA AUC or generalisation-gap values. The excerpted evidence does not provide sample counts or repeated-run variability for these measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No other numeric results were extracted: the detection accuracy, F1 scores, and detection-round results evaluate the paper’s proposed detection mechanisms, rather than the claim’s random-label behavior. Figure-only plots were not used to infer values.

untested.parts: Completely random training labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for real and random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Zero-error fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a full random-label corruption sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T3 classification with discusses/T6. The original random-label paper is cited in Appendix C to interpret memorisation, without a test or operational use of its specific random-label finding. Detection performance and utility-cost results do not supply missing evidence for V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, chance test error, and whether architecture or training hyperparameters must change.
Training-time cost of fitting random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Training and test error across a sweep from no label corruption to fully random labels.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation affect random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.
